The US Open. This name refers to two major championships, both held annually in the United States: one in tennis and one in golf.

In tennis, the US Open is held in late August and early September at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows in Queens, New York. Played on DecoTurf hard courts, it is the fastest surface of all four Grand Slam tournaments. This speed produces high-scoring games and favors aggressive playing styles that reward service power and quick volleys, distinguishing the US Open from the clay courts of the French Open or the grass courts of Wimbledon.

The tennis tournament moved to its current location in nineteen seventy eight and has been held there continuously, making it the longest running major at one venue. Billie Jean King's name was added to the USTA facility in two thousand six, honoring her pioneering contributions to tennis and her work championing equal opportunity in sports. Serena Williams has won the most US Open tennis titles with six singles championships, dominating the American major throughout her career. Roger Federer won five US Open tennis titles and was one of the tournament's dominant players in the two thousands.

In golf, the US Open is held in June and rotates among courses approved by the United States Golf Association, known for its difficulty and championship level challenge. Tiger Woods has won the golf US Open three times and is one of the few golfers to capture multiple major championships at this event. Jack Nicklaus won the golf US Open four times and holds the record for the most major championships overall in professional golf, a record that has stood for decades and defines his legacy.
